title: Yuezhi migration from Gansu to Bactria
summary: Defeated by the Xiongnu, the Yuezhi left Gansu in 162 BCE and moved some 2,000 km northwest to the Ili Valley and Ysyk Kul, displacing the Sai. About three decades later, in 132 BCE, the Wusun attacked them and they moved on through Ferghana and Sogdia to northern Bactria, which the Chinese called Daxia, north of the Amu Darya.

uncertainty.note: Benjamin (2003): left the Gansu in 162; Wusun attack in 132 BCE; perhaps winter 132/131 BCE in southwestern Ferghana and perhaps spring 131 BCE into Kangju (Sogdia); occupation of the lands north of the Amu Darya about thirty years after the start. Hill gives no date for the move to Daxia. Years are astronomical (162 BCE = -161); end is the last dated waypoint.

as_recorded.value: Leaving the Gansu in 162 the Yuezhi headed northwest towards the Ili Valley
In 132 BCE the Kunmo led a powerful force of mounted Wusun archers into the region
Perhaps in the spring of 131 BCE then, the Yuezhi most probably moved from Ferghana into the 'state' of Kangju

where.modern_name: Route from the Hexi Corridor (Gansu, China) to Ysyk Kul (Kyrgyzstan), the Ferghana Valley, Sogdia and northern Afghanistan
where.historical_name: Gansu under the Xiongnu; then Sai lands in the Ili, Dayuan (Ferghana), Kangju (Sogdia) and the former Greek kingdom of Bactria (Daxia)

waypoints.label: Hexi Corridor, Gansu: the Yuezhi, defeated by the Xiongnu, set out northwest in 162 BCE.

waypoints.date: After 162 BCE (Benjamin: settling near Ysyk Kul; no year of arrival given)
waypoints.label: Ili Valley and Ysyk Kul (Issyk-Kul): the Yuezhi displaced the Sai and stayed almost three decades; the Wusun attack came in 132 BCE.
Dayuan, identified with the Ferghana Valley, where the Yuezhi met little resistance.
Kangju, identified with Sogdia and probably the Zeravshan Valley.

waypoints.date: Undated here (Benjamin: about thirty years after leaving Gansu)
waypoints.label: Bactria (Daxia), the lands north of the Amu Darya; Hill: the Yuezhi moved to Daxia and divided it among five xihou.

importance.justification: A long nomad migration across Central Asia that put the Yuezhi in Bactria, where later Han envoys found them.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the Bactria leg: Benjamin gives it only as thirty years later and Hill gives no date, so that waypoint is undated. Dates for Ferghana and Sogdia are hedged "perhaps" by Benjamin, and the Wikidata points for Sogdia and the Ferghana Valley are regional centres; the pin is the Ferghana Valley point. The id says 162; I read it as 162 BCE per Benjamin.

beats.caption: Defeated by the Xiongnu, the Yuezhi leave Gansu and head northwest toward the Ili Valley and Ysyk Kul, about 2,000 km away.
The Wusun, led by their Kunmo, attack the Yuezhi in the Ili and force them to move west again.
The Yuezhi pass through Ferghana into Sogdia and on to Bactria (Daxia), which they later divide among five xihou.
